scanner_meta.name: Outpost Perimeter Asteroid Trail-Cam & UAP Bogey Detector
scanner_meta.location: High Basalt Shelf Perimeter Rim & Tower Mast, Asteroid 3-5-1 (Oort Cloud Sector 9)
scanner_meta.description: Motion-triggered optical, starlight-CMOS, and white-hot FLIR trail-cameras deployed around Outpost Nine to detect stray Oort boulders and cometary ice shards—routinely triggered by non-ballistic Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) stalking the relay array.

sightings.title: The Acheron Specular Cylinder ('Tic-Tac')
sightings.subtitle: Stationary Mirror-Capsule Hovering Between Tumbling Basalt Boulders
sightings.sensor_mode: STARLIGHT CMOS MONOCHROME • ISO 51,200 + IONIZATION HALO FILTER

coupling.hauser_rf_effect: Induced -1,420 Hz phase-notch on 21-cm H-I Maser Preamp
coupling.vector_signature: +140g Instantaneous Vertical Departure • Zero Propellant Plume

sightings.narrative: Trail-Cam TRL-01 triggered when two ordinary carbonaceous boulders (1.4 m/s ballistic drift) crossed the north guy-wire motion gate. Hovering dead-still between the two tumbling rocks was a 6.2-meter featureless mirror-chrome cylinder with a faint cyan Cherenkov tip-halo. On Frame 06/08, the cylinder departed vertically at >140g with zero propellant plume.
sightings.bureau_coverup: SECTOR 9 SAFETY BOARD NOTE: 'Misidentified stainless-steel thermos flask vented from Mess Hall airlock.'

sightings.narrative: Triggered by outgassing Oort comet shard C/2736-K4 drifting 1.8 km west of the shelf. Tucked inside the comet's cold sublimation plume was a dark-faceted object matching the boulder's roll rate to 0.001 rad/s—until Frame 05/08, when it executed an unbanked 90.00° right-angle turn across the camera field.
sightings.bureau_coverup: SECTOR 9 SAFETY BOARD NOTE: 'Detached radar calibration corner-reflector from Silicate Quarry 44-K.'

Upward mast camera TRL-09 caught three translucent plasmoid spheres perched directly inside Apex Rings 2 and 3, extending coronal filaments onto the copper radiator to drink RF power until Reactor #2 stepped down.
